lines.trans: I heard Cindy got hurt—why are you injuring a cast member from somebody else's show?
Yeah, she got hurt because of me—she is in Room 1206, go on up and see her.
How clumsy can I get—you always knew I would cause an accident someday, right?
Stop talking like that—let me see where and how badly you hurt yourself.
Ugh, let go of my arm!
Clumsy me caused an accident and got your show's cast member injured.
I caused trouble for you and made you uncomfortable—I am truly sorry!
Hey—are you crying?
Please just leave me alone for a bit.
I am sorry about today.

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

meanings.note: Used for physical injuries

examples.trans: I fell and hurt my knee.
Be careful not to get hurt.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?
Did you hear about this someone else's?
I was busy today because of someone else's.

meanings.note: colloquial clipping of 프로그램
clipping of 프로페셔널

examples.trans: What shows are you watching these days?
That show has high viewership ratings.
Did you hear about this cast member?
I was busy today because of cast member.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 어 다쳤어, 걔 나 때문에 다쳤다, 1206호야 올라가 봐.
examples.trans: Yeah, she got hurt because of me—she is in Room 1206, go on up and see her.
Here the word for 'it is Room 1206' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 가위바위보에서 졌다고 신디가 짐도 다 들고 올라갔대요.
examples.trans: Because she lost rock-paper-scissors, they say Cindy carried all the bags up herself.
This expression comes from 'they say she went up'.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.en: how much / how many / how long
meanings.note: Asks about degree, amount, price, or duration

examples.trans: How much will the repair cost be?
How long does it take from here to the station?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 내가 얼마나 칠칠치 못하면, 너 언젠가 한번 사고 칠 줄 알았지?
examples.trans: How clumsy can I get—you always knew I would cause an accident someday, right?
This expression comes from 'neat, careful'.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 내가 얼마나 칠칠치 못하면, 너 언젠가 한번 사고 칠 줄 알았지?
examples.trans: How clumsy can I get—you always knew I would cause an accident someday, right?
Here the word for 'someday' is key.

meanings.note: Written as one word (한번) when softening a suggestion or request ('why don't we...').

examples.trans: Try eating this food.
Come visit sometime when you have time.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to cause (trouble)
meanings.note: Used in idioms like 사고를 치다 (to cause trouble).

examples.trans: I caused trouble.
I caused trouble. (2)

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Often used as a command or suggestion to stop.

examples.trans: Please stop now.
Let's stop fighting.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Ugh, let go of my arm!
Here the word for 'ugh' is key.

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.
Did you hear about this you guys?
I was busy today because of you guys.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 너한테 민폐 끼치고 너 불편하게 만들었다, 진짜 미안하다!
examples.trans: I caused trouble for you and made you uncomfortable—I am truly sorry!
Here the word for 'trouble, burden' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너한테 민폐 끼치고 너 불편하게 만들었다, 진짜 미안하다!
examples.trans: I caused trouble for you and made you uncomfortable—I am truly sorry!
This expression comes from 'causing and'.

불편하다.gloss: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient

meanings.en: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient
meanings.note: Describes physical discomfort, awkwardness, or inconvenience.

examples.trans: This chair is a bit uncomfortable.
Please let me know if anything is uncomfortable.
I want to making right now.
How about trying to making together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g. 우세요, 웁니다).

examples.trans: I cried because the movie was sad.
The baby is crying loudly.
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
